answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned through verifiable work history, like a meadow where every thread of trust is woven from completed transactions. An attacker facing a gale of fake accounts would need to pay the real cost of building that history for each one: time, fees, and attestations from independent peers, so creating thousands of cheap identities buys no influence. Reputation is expensive to grow and cheap to verify.
